Repo: <workspace> (Hono v4.13.18). You own exactly two files: `src/context.ts` and `src/context.test.ts`. Make all edits with the edit/write tools; do not run `git add`, `git stage`, or `git commit`. Leave changes unstaged.

GOAL
Fix header injection in `Context.redirect()` (around lines 768-780 of src/context.ts). Raw CR (`\r`, U+000D) and LF (`\n`, U+000A) in the `location` string must be percent-encoded as `%0D` and `%0A` in the outgoing `Location` header, while preserving all existing valid redirect behavior (plain paths, absolute URLs, multibyte encoding via encodeURI, and already-percent-encoded strings that must NOT be double-encoded).

IMPLEMENTATION
Current code:

```ts
const locationString = String(location)
this.header(
  'Location',
  // Multibytes should be encoded
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
  !/[^\x00-\xFF]/.test(locationString) ? locationString : encodeURI(locationString)
)
```

Change it so the value passed to `this.header()` additionally replaces every literal CR and LF character with `%0D` / `%0A` after the existing multibyte decision. For example, compute the header value once, then `.replace(/[\r\n]/g, (char) => (char === '\r' ? '%0D' : '%0A'))`. Do not use encodeURIComponent on the whole URL (that would break URLs), and do not alter the existing `[^\x00-\xFF]` / `encodeURI` logic or the `no-control-regex` eslint comment placement. Keep the diff minimal and in the project's existing formatting style (no semicolons, single quotes, 100/120-col style already in file).

Keep in mind: `encodeURI` already encodes actual CR/LF, so when the multibyte branch is taken the replace is effectively a no-op there; the replace is what protects the non-multibyte branch.

TESTS
